goal: Split src/db.ts (1541 lines) and src/server.ts (1148 lines) into domain-scoped modules with no observable change: src/db.ts becomes a re-export barrel over src/db/{connection,schema,flights,trips,plannedLegs,settings}.ts, and src/server.ts keeps only middleware wiring, /api/status, the SPA catch-all and the error handler, with every other handler moved into express Router factories in src/routes/{flights,trips,plannedLegs,settings,exports}.ts (plus src/routes/uploads.ts for the two multer instances). No schema change, no new or changed HTTP endpoint, no ORM, no new dependency, and src/flightManager.ts is not touched. Correctness is proved by two machine-checkable baselines captured before any code moves — the ordered (method, full path) route table of the real app, and the sorted list of names exported by dist/db.js — plus differential curl against a pristine git worktree of the pre-refactor tree running on a second port.
frozen_decisions: USER (verbatim, user_stories/refactor.md): Database Layer — Create and migrate database concerns into: db/flights.ts, db/trips.ts, db/plannedLegs.ts, db/settings.ts.
USER (verbatim, user_stories/refactor.md): Routing Layer — Create and migrate HTTP route concerns into routers for: flights, trips, plannedLegs, settings, exports.

USER (verbatim, user_stories/refactor.md): Do not introduce an ORM. Do not introduce a complex/new architecture. Do not change the role of FlightManager as domain/state-machine logic. Preserve existing behavior and API contracts. Prefer straightforward file/module extraction over redesign. Application behavior remains functionally equivalent.

ORCHESTRATOR (verbatim): db.ts's auth/session functions (getAuthUser, setAuthUser, getAppSecret, getOrCreateAppSecret, getSetting, setSetting, sessionGet, sessionSet, sessionDestroy, sessionSweep — currently lines ~1440-1541) have no dedicated target file in the spec's DB list, so they land in db/settings.ts alongside the settings table.
ORCHESTRATOR (verbatim): tasks that touch the same file must be sequenced, not parallel.

PLANNER FREEZE — src/db.ts survives as a thin re-export barrel (no SQL, no logic, target <= 40 lines). It is NOT deleted and src/db/index.ts is NOT created: eleven call sites import './db' or '../db', and three test files do vi.mock('../src/db', ...) against the ten functions src/flightManager.ts imports. Keeping db.ts as the barrel means every one of those keeps resolving to exactly the same specifier with zero edits and zero resolution ambiguity (TypeScript, Node and Vite all resolve ./db to db.ts before db/).

PLANNER FREEZE — the sqlite handle lives in src/db/connection.ts only (module-level `let db`, initDb, closeDb, getDb, DB_PATH). Every extracted db module calls getDb() INSIDE each function body; no module may capture the handle, a prepared statement, or a transaction at module load, because initDb() runs after import.

PLANNER FREEZE — db modules own FUNCTIONS, not tables. A module's SQL may read or write any table (deleteTrip/assignFlightToTrip legitimately UPDATE flights and JOIN planned_legs; combineFlights only ever touches flights/flight_points and therefore belongs to db/flights.ts). No db domain module may import another db domain module; the only permitted intra-db import is ./connection. This is what keeps the split free of cycles.

PLANNER FREEZE — routers are factories returning express.Router (createFlightsRouter(flightManager), createTripsRouter(flightManager), createPlannedLegsRouter(flightManager), createSettingsRouter(), createExportsRouter()), following the existing precedent of createIngestRouter (src/ingest.ts:124) and createAuthRouter (src/auth/routes.ts:11).

PLANNER FREEZE — all five routers mount at '/api' with paths declared relative to it (router.get('/flights/:id', ...)), in this order and nowhere else in the file: flights, trips, settings, plannedLegs, exports — i.e. each router is mounted at the exact position in createServer() that its inline block occupies today. Every mount stays below `app.use('/api', requireAuth)` (server.ts:221) and above `app.get('*')` (server.ts:1114), which is the constraint the comments at server.ts:571-573 and 700-702 are protecting.

PLANNER FREEZE — server.ts:165-221 (express.json, static, TrafficStore, the /api/ingest mount above the session middleware, the session secret, session(), requireSameOrigin, the /api/auth mount, the /api ingest gate) is not reordered, reworded or moved. /api/status, app.get('*') and the final error-handling middleware also stay in server.ts.

PLANNER FREEZE — route modules import the specific db module they use (import { getFlights } from '../db/flights'), not the barrel. The barrel exists for backwards compatibility with flightManager/index/setPassword/backfills/inspectors/auth, not as the preferred path for new code. If a specific-module import would create a cycle, use '../db' instead and say so in the report.

PLANNER FREEZE — exports router owns exactly the five routes whose path ends in export.pdf or export.kml (server.ts:987-1113) and the private helpers they use (slugify, dateStamp, flightExportFilename, sendPdf, sendKml, includePlans, localeParams — server.ts:94-163). GET/POST/DELETE /api/flights/:id/flight-plan is flight-plan file management and stays in the flights router. /api/active-trip and /api/trips/:id/journey go to the trips router. PUT /api/flights/:id/planned-leg and PUT /api/flights/:id/planned-leg-status go to the plannedLegs router.
sequencing_rationale: Baselines before edits. The whole run is judged on 'functionally equivalent', so phase 1 first produces two artifacts that make that falsifiable: the ordered (method, full path) route table of the app createServer() actually builds, and the sorted export list of dist/db.js. Every later task diffs against them, and the final task diffs against them again. Without this the review is opinion.

DB before routes. Route modules import db functions; doing the db split first means each router is written once against its final import path. The reverse order would force a second edit of every router. The two layers are also kept in separate phases rather than run in parallel: a broken intermediate in one layer would make `npx tsc` output unreadable for the other, and both layers are backend so parallelism buys nothing but wall clock.

The same-file rule drives the task count. Every db task edits src/db.ts and every route task edits src/server.ts, so within a phase the tasks are a strict chain, never parallel. The only genuinely parallel pair in the run is T-001 (new file src/inspect-routes.ts + run artifacts) against T-002 (src/db*), whose paths are disjoint.

1541 lines is split across two tasks (T-002, T-003) rather than one, not for tidiness but because a single cold agent moving that much code in one turn is where silent omissions happen. The seam is chosen so each task ends in a tree that compiles, passes npm test, and has an unchanged export surface: T-002 lands connection/schema/flights/trips and converts every remaining bare `db.` in db.ts to getDb(); T-003 is then a pure move of the two remaining blocks.

The route phase is split three ways on the same principle, ordered easiest-seam-first so the mount pattern is proven cheaply before the 400-line planned-legs block moves: T-005 (uploads + settings + exports) establishes the '/api' mount and proves the app-level error handler still sees MulterError and the JSON SyntaxError from inside a router; T-006 moves flights + trips; T-007 moves planned legs and empties server.ts.

combineFlights (db.ts:646-779) is the one move with real numeric behavior — filler-point interpolation, ownDurationSec, haversine/bearing copies that geo.ts deliberately does not own. It is a differential-test target in T-002, not just a compile target.

Reviewer gates run at opus in all three phases: phase 1 relocates the schema and migration code and the deletion paths (deleteFlight/deleteTrip/deletePlannedLeg), phase 2 moves the routes that sit behind the auth gate including every DELETE endpoint, and phase 3 is the final acceptance sign-off.
No Designer. The run introduces no contract — no schema change, no new endpoint, no shared type. Every structural choice that would have been a design decision is frozen above instead.
